The two-role threshold sits exactly at the value that keeps the live reading green: at >= 1 the live reading fails on two enums. I accept the stated reason - both are the ['HUMAN','MODEL','WORKER','SYSTEM'] actor-kind taxonomy and grading them closed would be a false positive - and I am not calling the rule wrong. The one test that pins the threshold, test_a_vocabulary_admitting_two_roles_and_no_alternate_is_closed, asserts a three-proving-role vocabulary, so it constrains the rule to <= 3 and nothing constrains it to 2. Every count in the repair of a count defect is off by one, and the method that produced them has the same blindness the defect had. Measured at each revision by matching '^| `<name>`' against `ls scripts/sov_*.py`: d00f46a 38 listed / 22 unlisted of 60; 04b24e8 38 / 23 of 61; a3ac836 40 / 21 of 61. The commit message states 37 -> 39 listed and 24 -> 22 unlisted. The discrepancy is exactly sov_f2_gate.py, whose name contains a digit: a `sov_[a-z_]+\.py` pattern misses it and yields precisely the builder's 37/39. So the numbers came from a regex with the same class of blind spot as the EVIDENCE_PATH defect this commit repairs, and the pre-existing prose in contracts/counted-populations.json:165 ('It said thirty-seven against sixty ... lost track of twenty-three') carries the same off-by-one and is the likely source read instead of measured. Separately, the new prose replaces one stale number with an ungraded one: 'a couple of dozen do not' is a count claim spelled in words, so sov_counts.py `check` cannot grade it and `debt` does not even list it (I ran both; scripts/README.md appears in debt only at lines 3, 27 and 28). It is 21 today and nothing will notice when it stops being. On a page one commit downstream of 'grade every hand-written count in live prose', that is worth naming.

'the page was reviewed against its declared basis and the receipt re-recorded' is unattestable. The whole receipt is {artifact_digest, basis[{path,digest}], changed}; do_record writes the digest of the file as it currently stands and nothing else; review_state compares digests. No reviewer, no timestamp, no finding, no basis for the verdict. The only bytes that moved in 0145727 are the artifact_digest. A real review and `sha256sum` produce byte-identical receipts, so the record cannot distinguish them, and this witness cannot either. Pre-existing repository design, not this branch's invention - recorded because the builder cited the receipt as evidence that a review happened, and it is not.

A second participant reading the landed repository cannot resolve the record of the refusal. Note the asymmetry the branch created for itself: an unresolvable address in `stage_observed_by` is a defect the reader raises, and the same address in `note` is read by nothing. This record has the same defect by construction, since I was directed to write under .local/ to keep the branch landable; the seam is real and belongs to whoever decides where witness records live, not to this concern.
